transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-23   Time: 15:00 PDT   Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Alex (Stillwater CTO), Priya (Infra), Jordan (ML Eng)
Links shared: pricing draft (redwood.com/shared/pricing-draft), security whitepaper (redwood.com/sec/whitepaper), benchmark sheet (drive/Stillwater/benchmarks)

Summary:
Stillwater is evaluating options to move away from a multi-vendor setup (OpenAI + in-house vLLM) toward a single serving platform that gives them predictable latency and cost. Primary concerns: inference parity vs their TGI/vLLM pipelines, private deployment/networking (VPC + on-prem), and enterprise security (SAML, KMS). They want an initial benchmark that replicates their 1k-10k token conversational workload and cost/latency baselines.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Thanks everyone for joining, we really appreciate the time. Quick roll call — and Connor's going to jump into technical details after I cover the high level.
[00:12] Alex (Stillwater): Yep hey, Alex here. We're excited to compare notes. We run a hybrid today; OpenAI for customer-facing features and a homegrown stack running vLLM/TGI for low-latency internal workflows.
[00:22] Priya (Stillwater): Priya here — I'm focused on security and network. We have strict egress controls and a VPC peering requirement for any prod traffic.
[00:29] Jordan (Stillwater): Jordan — ML infra, I run the current TGI tests and orchestration.
[00:35] Connor (Redwood): Connor — I'll pick up on the serving/runtime questions, particularly around KV cache behavior and batching.

[01:05] Maya: High level, our customers typically pick one of three modes: hosted (fastest to get started), dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or private (VPC or on-prem). Curious where you're leaning?
[01:18] Alex: For the short list we want the option of dedicated to start for predictable latency, but also evaluate private because of compliance in a couple of EU customers. We also want to understand what parity looks like with our TGI pipelines.
[01:30] Maya: Totally — parity is a common ask. Connor, do you want to take the parity / runtime nuance?

[01:37] Connor: Sure. Two vectors: functional parity (outputs, tokens) and performance parity (latency/throughput). For functional parity we focus on model variant compatibility and tokenizer differences — sometimes small tokenization changes can shift prompts. For performance, we look at KV cache semantics, continuous batching, and kernel selection. A lot of teams run v L L M locally with custom kernels; we mirror those optimizations in our runtime but there are edge cases.
[02:05] Jordan: Quick one — our current TGI setup pins a custom 4-bit quant and a patched attention kernel. How do you handle quant profiles?
[02:13] Connor: We support quantized variants and have quant profiles per model/instance. We also provide recommendations — some workloads prefer 4-bit QAT vs static quantization. There will be cases where exact bitwise parity isn't identical, but we aim for output parity within your eval tolerance.

[02:45] Priya: Security — what about key management? KMS/H S M? We can't have keys leaving our cloud account for private deployments.
[02:55] Maya: For private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, plus private control plane options. For dedicated/hosted we offer envelope encryption and managed KMS with strict retention policies — we'll send the SOC2 / ISO docs.
[03:12] Alex: Also need audit logs at token level for certain flows. Does Redwood expose token-level audit/tracing?
[03:20] Connor: Yes — Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route traces. For private, logs can be forwarded into your SIEM or stored in your S3 bucket.

[03:50] Jordan: On the latency vs cost tradeoff: we often prefer slightly higher latency if token cost is ~30% lower. Can you tune batching and caching per route?
[04:00] Connor: Absolutely. We expose routing policies and per-route SLOs. You can set aggressive batching for non-interactive routes and low-latency configs for customer-facing endpoints. There's also automatic prefix/KV caching. We can show historical token savings from similar customers.

[04:30] Alex: How big a lift is migration? We're tied into OpenAI APIs for some product pieces and vLLM for others; we don't want two parallel maintenance efforts.
[04:40] Maya: Migration is usually a phased approach: port a subset of models + routes, run benchmark parity tests, then cutover. We'll help with SDK shims and a compatibility checklist. Typical teams do a canary and 2-week burn-in.

[05:05] Priya: Networking specifics — we need private endpoints, no public egress allowed from model servers. Is that supported?
[05:14] Connor: Yes — in Private mode you get customer-managed networks, private endpoints, and optional on-prem packaging. Dedicated also supports VPC peering depending on region/contract. We'll share the network diagrams.

[05:40] Jordan: For benchmarking, we want to run our conversational set: 70% short (50–150 tokens), 25% mid (200–1k tokens), 5% long (2k–6k tokens). Also we use custom sampling and top-p tweaks. Can Redwood run with identical sampling seeds?
[05:58] Connor: Seeds and sampling hyperparams are supported. We'll attempt to reproduce your sampling config and run both TGI and Redwood-hosted models side-by-side. Expect small stochastic variance but we measure divergence metrics and perplexity where applicable.

[06:20] Alex: What about cost accounting? We bill tokens, but our infra folks want a per-route per-token breakdown down to cents.
[06:30] Maya: The Console gives token-level billing and we can export attribution to your billing systems. For Dedicated we can also provide committed rate cards so unit economics are predictable.

[06:50] Priya: Compliance: does Redwood support SSO via SAML/Okta and SCIM?
[06:57] Maya: Yes, SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning are supported, plus RBAC roles and audit trails. We also have enterprise contracts with custom DPA/processing addenda.

[07:20] Jordan: A nit — some vendors change tokenizer behavior between versions which breaks our prompt engineering. How do you handle version pinning?
[07:29] Connor: You can pin model versions per-route. The platform also supports rollout policies for canary and A/B testing so you can validate tokenizer drift before global switch.

[07:55] Alex: Competitor question — how do you handle functions/tool-calls for structured outputs? Our product uses tool-calling heavily.
[08:03] Connor: We support tool/function calling with structured output enforcement and schema validation. We also integrate tracing so you can see which tool calls triggered which model tokens.

[08:30] Maya: Operational question — if we go dedicated, what's the SLA and what does escalation look like?
[08:38] Maya: (continues) We provide SLA-backed latency targets and uptime for Dedicated customers. Enterprise contracts include named support contacts, on-call escalation, and optional runbooks.

[09:05] Priya: Cost example request — show us a 3-tier cost breakdown: hosted, dedicated monthly commit, and private on our infra.
[09:12] Maya: We'll produce that. We'll also include a recommended dedicated sizing config given your current throughput numbers.

[09:35] Jordan: Back to parity — any public cases where you had to match a custom vLLM kernel?
[09:43] Connor: Yeah, we've worked with teams that had custom kernel patches. Usually we either add a custom kernel path or show that our runtime with specific quantization and kernel selection matches within your eval thresholds. We'll include examples in the benchmark plan.

[10:10] -- brief mute/sidetalk for 90s --

[12:00] Alex: Ok real ask: can we run an A/B for two weeks with 10% traffic to Redwood Hosted to see production behavior?
[12:10] Maya: Yes, that's a common approach. For data residency and egress concerns, we'd ensure traffic routing matches your policies.

[12:30] Priya: A couple of red flags: we need explicit data retention terms and a way to purge logs for regulatory requests.
[12:38] Maya: Understood — we'll include purge workflows and retention policies in the security docs.

[13:00] Jordan: On instrumentation — do you export traces to Jaeger/Zipkin?
[13:08] Connor: We integrate with common tracing stacks and can emit spans to your tracing backend, and provide per-request metadata for debugging.

[13:30] Alex: Who else at Redwood do we need to talk to for procurement and legal?
[13:36] Maya: I'll introduce you to our sales ops and legal once you want a dedicated quote. For security deep dives we can schedule a SOC2/arch review with our security lead.

[13:55] Alex: Great. Anything else on the tech side?
[14:00] Jordan: One last: how do you handle multi-tenant isolation on Dedicated?
[14:07] Connor: Dedicated is physically separated GPU pools per account; we also offer tenant-level isolation inside those pools plus strict resource quotas and network segmentation.

[14:30] Maya: Quick recap and next steps: we'll send the pricing matrix and security whitepaper. Connor will share a benchmark plan and perf script. You'll share prompt sets and token distribution. Then we schedule a two-hour sanity benchmark and a week-long parity run.

[14:58] Alex: That sounds good. Possible timeline: we want initial numbers within two weeks so leadership can decide.

[15:10] Maya: We'll aim to have the cost/benchmark plan in 3 business days and the perf scripts in a week — confirmed in the action items.

Wrap-up notes:
- Shared artifacts: pricing draft link, security whitepaper link, benchmark sheet link (customer to upload prompts)
- Next meeting: benchmark kickoff (2 hours) targeted for week of 2027-08-02

[15:40] End meeting.
